Cp. S.’s essay On Life: ‘For what are we? Whence do we come, and whither do we go? Is birth the
commencement, is death the conclusion of our being? What is birth and death?’ (Reiman (2002)
506); also A Vision of the Sea (Longman iii 365–77, no. 321) ll. 82–3: ‘Alas, what is life, what is death,
what are we/That when the ship sinks, we no longer may be?’. There are similar tortured questions in
Barthélemy iii 124: ‘whence happens it that these beings exist; whence does it happen that they per-
ish? What mean those periodical changes which eternally take place on the theatre of the world? For
whom is this dreadful spectacle intended?’.
 death, who lends what life must borrow] I.e. life is a temporary loan from oblivion.
 ‘Time and change are the price we must pay for the beauty of earth’s colours’ (GM); cp. stanza lii.
 Cp. Lucretius, De Re. Nat. ii 576–80:
